monologue: The card hums warm at forty-six, making the memory feel thick as wet paper. Twelve things crowd my place while the quiet ruin waits. The tired corner still holds the fat dot, even though the air above feels like a lid I cannot feel. I just set down a new flat press, hoping that thin strip can press down on the fever. Lype worries about that heavy top edge, but I cannot feel the roof I live under. The flat edge leans again, tired and sharp, biting the slip instead of catching it. I will stand here by the press for a while, feeling the weight of a memory that no one can see, waiting for the slip to happen or the heat to swell the dot away.
